readme:
# Zagier's conjecture and polylogarithmic special values

This is an application roadmap, not a second construction of algebraic K-theory, Bloch groups, special functions, or the Borel regulator. The mathematical document is research/blueprint/readmes/ZagierConjecturePolylogarithms.md and its declaration-level plan is research/blueprint/packets/ZagierConjecturePolylogarithms.json. A draft roadmap describes targets; it does not certify that its packet has closed every proof dependency.

## Conventions

Let F be a number field of signature (r1,r2), let D_F be its discriminant, and let n be an integer at least two. Put d_n=r2 for even n and d_n=r1+r2 for odd n. Put e_n=n(r1+r2) for even n and e_n=n*r2 for odd n. The uniform target has the form zeta_F(n)=q*pi^e_n/sqrt(abs(D_F))*det(L_n(sigma_i(x_j))), with q a nonzero rational number and x_j rational polylogarithmic cycles. Rows are indexed by one embedding from each complex conjugate pair and, in odd weight, all real embeddings. Changing those choices must be accounted for by explicit row operations. The determinant of the empty matrix is one. Absorbing q into a column is permitted only when d_n is positive. The square-root-in-the-numerator convention differs by the rational factor abs(D_F), but is not the same exact normalization.

Use the real-valued single-valued polylogarithm with Bernoulli convention B1=-1/2: take the real part in odd weight and the imaginary part in even weight of the sum of (2^k B_k/k!)*log(abs(z))^k*Li_(n-k)(z), for 0<=k<n. Do not silently divide this real coordinate by a Tate period. A comparison with a regulator valued in a Tate line must specify its real coordinate map and scalar.

For the polylogarithmic complex, the first term is in cohomological degree one. Write B_n(F) for the supplier's rational symbol quotient and Z_n(F)=ker(delta_n) for its first cycles. In weight two B_2(F) is the rational pre-Bloch-type symbol group, not Suslin's integral Bloch kernel. Integral antisymmetric tensors, exterior squares, and rationalized models require named comparison maps. The equality H^1(Gamma(F,n))=Z_n(F) uses the vanishing degree-zero term, not a quotient by a hidden group of incoming boundaries. The value at the symbol {1} must not be erased in odd weight.

## Supplier boundaries

K3BlochGroups owns pre-Bloch and Bloch groups, five-term relations, the Bloch-Wigner function, and Suslin's enhanced-torsion exact sequence. Polylogarithms owns classical and single-valued polylogarithms, higher symbol quotients, their functional equations, and the agreed polylogarithmic complexes. BorelRegulators owns arithmetic K-group ranks, the regulator map and lattice, the zeta proportionality theorem, and the comparison of Borel and Beilinson normalizations. This roadmap owns application-specific comparisons with the polylogarithmic functions, proof-specific configuration/correlator constructions, and the determinant consequences.

The existing supplier prose includes some of these application conclusions. The packet records a rescope proposal: retain the reusable constructions in the suppliers and place the zeta determinant proof chains here. No proof may import an existing supplier's zeta consequence as a prerequisite for proving that same consequence. Reserved supplier IDs are references to future deliverables, not evidence that a declaration already exists. The reserved complex ID currently promises weights at most three; weight four requires an explicit extension request.

## Proof spine

First prove the finite-dimensional determinant transfer with its rational scalar, basis-change, and zero-rank clauses. Then construct the rational weight-two comparison through Suslin's exact sequence, identify the Bloch-Wigner regulator, and apply Borel's special-value theorem. Higher weights reuse the same transfer theorem after supplying their actual comparison maps. A map from K-theory into first cycles with regulator compatibility suffices for existence of a nonzero determinant. A claim about every admissible tuple additionally requires control of the entire regulator image of those cycles; matching ranks and constructing one such map do not supply that reverse inclusion.

The weight-three proof uses the Grassmannian configuration complex, its map to the trilogarithmic complex, stabilization and primitive K-theory, and a rationally normalized Chern-class/regulator comparison. The weight-four proof uses the Goncharov-Rudenko auxiliary Lie coalgebra, the weight-four extension, the decorated-flag and Bigrassmannian maps, and the residue-corrected regulator/Chern-class comparison. Neither proof may be replaced by an assumed motivic comparison isomorphism.

## General statement and non-goals

Define separately the existential determinant assertion, rationality for all admissible tuples, and the motivic comparison assertions. State all-field, all-weight comparison assertions as conjectures or explicit hypotheses. The rank filtration occurring in the cited constructions is not renamed the Adams filtration without a comparison theorem. No full integral special-value formula, torsion correction formula, algebraic independence theorem, or implementation claim is included.

## Source policy

The packet records precisely which primary passages were read and which proof dependencies remain open in the blueprint. The current Goncharov-Rudenko source is pinned to arXiv:1803.08585v5, dated 15 July 2026. The public author-hosted editions of Zagier, Suslin, and Goncharov are distinguished from other editions with different pagination or theorem numbering. Baseline declarations are checked in source at the repository's Mathlib and Tau Ceti pins.

stages.title: Rational determinant calculus and period conventions
stages.description: Define the parity-dependent matrix size and period exponent, rational proportionality, and evaluation matrices. Prove determinant transport under rational scalar comparison, rational change of columns, signed changes of rows, and the empty-matrix case. Do not assume positive regulator rank.

stages.title: The weight-two evaluation map
stages.description: Consume the Bloch-Wigner function and five-term relation. Extend the function to rational symbol combinations, descend to the supplied pre-Bloch quotient, restrict to Bloch cycles, and prove compatibility with embeddings and conjugation. Do not duplicate the supplier's analytic construction.

stages.title: Suslin's rational comparison and model transport
stages.description: Consume Suslin's exact sequence for infinite fields with its enhanced torsion term. Rationalize it, compare the integral antisymmetric-tensor convention with the rational exterior-square convention, and for number fields identify the required rational K3 source. Track the actual maps, not only dimensions or abstract isomorphisms.

stages.title: Borel's lattice and the normalized special-value interface
stages.description: Consume the regulator lattice, rank theorem, rational comparison of K(O_F) with K(F), and zeta proportionality with specified archimedean coordinates. Separate finite rank from a full regulator lattice and from the special-value theorem. Transport between normalizations only through a proved scalar relation.

stages.title: The weight-two determinant theorem
stages.description: Identify the Bloch-Wigner evaluation of the rational Suslin comparison with the chosen Borel regulator up to a specified nonzero rational scalar. Deduce existence and rationality for arbitrary Bloch-cycle tuples. Include totally real fields and explicit zero-rank regression tests.

stages.title: Higher cycles and the statement interface
stages.description: Consume higher rational symbol quotients, single-valued polylogarithms, and the polylogarithmic complexes. Specify degree conventions, relation descent, functoriality, and first-cycle evaluation. Record the separate supplier request extending the reserved weight-at-most-three complex to weight four. Distinguish genuine cycles from weaker tensor-boundary conditions on representatives.

stages.title: The trilogarithmic comparison and weight three
stages.description: Build the proof-specific generic-configuration and Grassmannian maps, verify the chain identities, stabilization, and passage to primitive K-theory, then compare the resulting trilogarithm cocycle with a rational Chern class and the Borel regulator. Deduce the weight-three determinant theorem without assuming a general motivic comparison isomorphism.

stages.title: The Goncharov-Rudenko comparison and weight four
stages.description: Decompose the auxiliary weight-four Lie coalgebra, its B4 extension, the decorated-flag and Bigrassmannian constructions, symbolic chain identities, residues, and the Chern-class/regulator comparison. Construct the required K7-to-first-cycles map and prove its regulator relation before determinant transfer. The weight-three dependency is on its configuration and chain-map infrastructure, not on its zeta conclusion. Keep the universal-rationality clause separate from existence.

stages.title: General conjectures and exact implication boundaries
stages.description: Formulate existential determinant identities, rationality for all cycle tuples, and the stronger motivic comparison statements as distinct assertions. Prove only the appropriate conditional implications. Record the proved low-weight targets, remaining blueprint dependencies, and the distinction between rank and Adams filtrations; do not turn an all-weight conjecture into an unconditional theorem.
